Elon Musk on why he bought Twitter and why free speech matters:

"I think we need to be very cautious about anything that results in the suppression of free speech."

Musk argues that one of the biggest dangers is creating an environment where people feel they can't question certain ideas, even questioning them becomes unacceptable.

He compares this to cancel culture, saying he has faced attempts to cancel him from both the left and the right.

Musk also emphasized why free speech is so important:

"Free speech is actually extremely important."

He pointed to the First Amendment and why it exists in the first place: people came to America from countries where speaking freely could get you imprisoned.

His broader message is simple:

A society cannot remain free if people are afraid to question ideas or speak openly.

TESLA: Cybercab Fleet Lot, Houston, TX, 8-8-2026

Saturday, August 8th, was a very busy day of Cybercab & Robotaxi testing at Houston's Fleet Lot, as well as the Tesla Hempstead Center.

Difficult to count how many Cybercabs were here due to the constant ins and outs of the fleet. If I had to guess, +140.

I spotted at least 3 Starlink enabled cabs and multiple with the Starlink indention, ready for a mount. The calibration Cybercab was also in use today as well.

If you notice, at one point there was either a shift change or break where employees formed a line and were being handed something from the back of a Model Y.  

There is a large 37 pic, 3 vid, Subscriber Photo-Thread attached! So sub and check it out.

Enjoy!

Elon Musk explains how Starlink works 

“So there are laser links between the satellites. So it forms sort of a laser mesh, so that if, let’s say if cables are damaged or cut, like fiber cables, the satellites can communicate between each other and provide connectivity. For example, when the Red Sea cables were cut… the Starlink satellite network continued to function.”
